summary.name: BrowBro
summary.one_liner: A free, open source macOS menu-bar app that intercepts clicked links and shows a small picker at your cursor to choose which browser or Chrome profile opens them.
use_cases: Pick which browser opens a link clicked in Messages or other apps
Send links to a specific Chrome profile (work vs personal)
Open links in private windows or Tor Browser on demand
Keep Safari as default while routing some links elsewhere
Quickly reorder and hide browsers in a link picker
summary.what_it_does: BrowBro becomes the default browser and catches link clicks system-wide. A compact picker then appears at the cursor, where you choose a browser or a specific Chrome profile by mouse or keyboard (1-9 quick keys, first letter, arrow keys, Enter). In Settings you can toggle which browsers and Chrome profiles appear and drag to reorder them. During setup it remembers your previous default so you can restore it in one click. The page says all routing happens locally on the Mac.
notable: Chrome profiles listed as separate targets with their color and email
Available as signed and notarized DMG, Homebrew cask, or Mac App Store build
Native Swift + SwiftUI, open source on GitHub
caveats: Switching between download channels resets settings and permissions
Mac App Store build is sandboxed and asks for Chrome folder access differently than the direct build
